## Launch from the project root

```bash
uv sync
uv run streamlit run app.py
```

Leave the terminal open. Ctrl+C stops the server. Streamlit scripts run through the terminal, rather than as ordinary notebook cells.

## Display information

```python
import streamlit as st

st.title("Conference Message Explorer")
st.header("Explore the sample")
st.subheader("Read a message")
st.write("Text, numbers, or other objects")
st.markdown("**Important context**")
st.caption("52 selected kickers, not the complete archive")
st.metric("Talks displayed", 16)
st.dataframe(df, hide_index=True)
```

`print(...)` writes to the server's terminal or logs. `st.write(...)` displays in the browser. Use explicit Streamlit display calls while learning.

## Inputs return Python values

```python
year = st.selectbox("Year", [2020, 2023, 2025])
years = st.multiselect("Years", [2020, 2023, 2025], default=[2025])
earliest = st.select_slider("Earliest year", [2020, 2023, 2025])
n = st.slider("Number to show", min_value=1, max_value=10, value=5)
text = st.text_input("Words in the title")
show_table = st.checkbox("Show supporting records", value=True)

shown = df.loc[df["year"].isin(years)]
if show_table:
    st.dataframe(shown)
```

In the basic execution model, committing a widget change reruns the script from top to bottom. A text input normally commits when the reader presses Enter or leaves the field. Plotly hover and zoom remain browser interactions unless the app explicitly connects supported events to Python.

## Charts

```python
st.bar_chart(shown.groupby("year").size().rename("Talks"))

import plotly.express as px
fig = px.scatter(shown, x="PHATE1", y="PHATE2",
                 color="role_group", hover_name="title")
st.plotly_chart(fig, width="stretch")

# For a Matplotlib or Seaborn figure:
st.pyplot(fig_matplotlib)
```

Plotly builds the interactive figure. Streamlit connects it to the rest of the app and to Python computations.

## Layout and supporting evidence

```python
with st.sidebar:
    year = st.selectbox("Year", [2020, 2023, 2025])

left, right = st.columns(2)
left.metric("Talks displayed", len(shown))
right.metric("Speakers represented", shown["speaker"].nunique())

with st.expander("Sources and interpretation"):
    st.write("Explain the sample, definitions, and limitations.")

st.link_button("Read the original talk", source_url)
```

An expander changes visibility. In the default behavior used here, putting code inside it does not make that computation wait until expansion.

## Empty results

```python
if shown.empty:
    st.info("No matches. Broaden your filters.")
    st.stop()
```

State clearly what an empty selection means. Apply the same filters to the map, metrics, and supporting records.

## Cache returned data

```python
@st.cache_data
def compute_map(X, random_state=386):
    print("CACHE MISS: fitting PHATE")
    return phate.PHATE(random_state=random_state).fit_transform(X)

coordinates = compute_map(X)
```

Matching function inputs and code can reuse a result. Changed inputs produce a different entry. The function call still occurs on a rerun, while a hit skips the body. Data caching returns copies. Default caches can be reused across users.

```python
@st.cache_data(ttl=600)  # seconds
def fetch_data(url):
    return pd.read_csv(url)

compute_map.clear()  # clear only this function's cached entries
```

Expiration affects a subsequent call. It does not schedule background data collection. A filename by itself does not capture changes in the file's contents. Our complete loader passes file bytes explicitly.

## Remember additional session values

```python
if "count" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.count = 0
if st.button("Add one"):
    st.session_state.count += 1
st.write(st.session_state.count)
```

| Need | Choose |
|---|---|
| Reuse a returned dataset or computation | `st.cache_data` |
| Reuse an in-process model or connection | `st.cache_resource` |
| Remember additional values for this session | `st.session_state` |
| Keep processed outputs across restarts | A saved, versioned data artifact |

Resource caching normally returns a shared object. Consider mutation and concurrent use. It does not cache the Ollama server's model process for you.

## Batch inputs with a form

```python
with st.form("request"):
    message = st.text_area("Message")
    submitted = st.form_submit_button("Analyze")

if submitted and message.strip():
    st.write(message)
```

The form submits its values together. Use it when running after every individual input change would be unhelpful.

## Deployment reminder

1. Run locally and check the original user task.
2. Commit code, data artifacts, `pyproject.toml`, and `uv.lock`.
3. At [share.streamlit.io](https://share.streamlit.io), select the repository, branch, and `app.py`.
4. Select Python 3.12, deploy, and check logs and access.
5. Commit and push changes to update the app.

GitHub stores the project. Community Cloud runs Python. GitHub Pages hosts the static website and can link to the app. Keep credentials out of Git. This demo needs none.
